analysis.title: Prime Perspective: Spike in ETF shorts confirms increased hedging yesterday. But single name activity does not point to signs of panic.
key_insights: Global Fundamental L/S hedge funds fell -1.3% on 11/5 (a -2 SD move), driven mainly by market/beta exposure. YTD performance is now +8.7%.
TMT L/S funds fell more than -4% and are now roughly flat to slightly positive YTD, down from about +24% before the June/July AI sell-off. US-focused funds fell -1.7% and are up 5.5% YTD.
Systematic L/S managers gained +0.2% and are up +16% YTD. Multi-Strats fell -1.4%, driven by high-beta names, Info Tech, Momentum (down 3.7 SD) and negative idiosyncratic returns.
GS's Vol Panic Index surged to 9.57 out of 10, back in the panic zone (9.5+). The ~5pt increase was the 3rd largest daily jump ever, and the combined two-day swing was the largest on record.
VVIX had the 2nd largest one-day increase ever, behind only Feb 2018 'Volmageddon'. Cboe put volume exceeded 11mm contracts, a record, surpassing the prior high in Apr 2025.

NDX fell -6.4% (worst 1-day drawdown since 3/16/20), R2K fell -4.5% (worst since 4/3/25) and SPX fell -4.4% (worst since 4/4/25). Many GS AI-related baskets had their biggest down day since the launch of ChatGPT.

The desk reads Prime flows as increased hedging via macro products but no sign of panic or accelerating de-grossing in single stocks. It concludes discretionary HFs were not the main driver of the price action.
US-listed ETF shorts rose +7%, the largest 1-day increase since March and the third largest in five years, led by Large Cap Equity ETFs.

Global equities were de-grossed for a 4th straight session (8 of last 9), but the pace was modest (-0.5 SD 1-year). Net selling was the largest in two weeks (-1.6 SD), driven by long-and-short sales at 2.2 to 1.

Nearly all regions were net sold except DM Asia, led by EM Asia (Taiwan, Korea, China), North America and Europe. 7 of 11 sectors were net sold, led by Info Tech, Consumer Disc and Industrials. Energy, Financials and Real Estate were the most net bought.

Global AI stocks (GSXGGLAI constituents) were net sold for a 6th straight session (-2.6 SD 1-year). The trailing 20-day pace of HF selling in AI stocks is the largest in more than five years (-3.0 SD 5-year).

HF gross leverage fell -0.7 pts to 314.2% (85th percentile 1-year, 97th 5-year). Net leverage fell -1.5 pts to 71.8% (4th percentile 1-year, 37th 5-year). Gross leverage ratio rose month/month because fund equity fell faster than gross market value.
risk_factors: Continued HF selling of global AI stocks, the largest 20-day pace in over five years.
Gross leverage ratio remains high (97th percentile 5-year) because fund equity is falling faster than gross market value.
Further erosion in TMT L/S fund performance after the -4% day.
vol_and_positioning: GS Vol Panic Index at 9.57/10, in the panic zone (9.5+). The ~5pt jump was the 3rd largest daily rise ever, following Wednesday's 4th largest drop ever.
VVIX posted its 2nd largest one-day increase ever, behind only Feb 2018.
Cboe put volume above 11mm contracts, the largest put volume day on record.
US-listed ETF shorts +7% in one day, the largest since March, led by Large Cap Equity ETFs. Desk reads this as macro-product hedging.
Global equity de-grossing for a 4th straight session at a modest pace (-0.5 SD 1-year). AI stocks net sold 6 sessions in a row (-2.6 SD 1-year).
HF gross leverage 314.2% (85th percentile 1-year, 97th percentile 5-year). Net leverage 71.8% (4th percentile 1-year, 37th percentile 5-year).

tension_points.bull_case: Single-stock Prime flows show no panic: de-grossing pace was modest (-0.5 SD 1-year), so discretionary HFs were not the main driver of the sell-off.
tension_points.bear_case: Vol Panic Index, VVIX, record put volume and the largest drawdowns since 2020 point to market stress, and HFs have been net selling AI stocks at the fastest 20-day pace in over five years.
tension_points.what_invalidates: An acceleration of single-stock de-grossing from the recent pace would undercut the no-panic read.

theme_stances.key_argument: Prime flows show increased hedging via macro products, but single-stock activity does not show panic or accelerating de-grossing.
theme_stances.evidence: they do NOT point to signs of panic and an acceleration of de- grossing activity
